questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook healthy vegan meals for the whole family
Why so many celebrities change their diets every year
How farmers raise cows and pigs for meat in the UK
Going vegan: the reasons for it and the difficulties
questions.why: They discuss what veganism is, why people choose it, and why not everyone can or will.

questions.q: According to Oxford University research, what could happen if people stopped eating meat and animal products?
options: Food prices would fall by 70%
Harmful emissions could fall by 70%
Farming jobs would increase
Electricity use would halve
questions.why: Neil says harmful emissions could be reduced by 70%, according to Oxford research.

questions.q: How does Tom Kuehnel from the Vegan Society describe veganism?
options: Simply a healthy diet without any meat, fish or eggs
A way to lose weight quickly and feel more energetic
Avoiding cruelty to animals in food, clothes and everything
A religion that started in the UK in the 1940s
questions.why: He says it excludes all exploitation and cruelty to animals, 'for food, clothing or any other purpose'.

questions.q: What does Tom Kuehnel say about being vegan today?
options: It has never been easier
It is very expensive
It is only possible in big cities
It is harder than in the past
questions.why: He says there are plenty of alternatives and 'it's never been easier to be vegan'.

questions.q: What health benefit did the Oxford scientists claim?
options: About 8 million deaths a year could be avoided
People would live 8 years longer
Half of all illnesses would disappear
Nobody would be overweight
questions.why: Catherine says they found 8 million deaths per year could be avoided if the world went vegan.

questions.q: What economic effect do the researchers suggest?
options: Farmers would earn more money from growing vegetables
Food would become much cheaper in supermarkets everywhere
Governments would collect more tax from meat companies
Up to $1,000bn a year saved in health costs and productivity
questions.why: They suggest up to $1,000bn a year could be saved from reduced healthcare costs and higher productivity.

questions.q: Why do the presenters mention the Berbers in the Sahara?
options: They are famous for their delicious traditional vegan food
They have stopped raising animals because of climate change
They live in dry areas where people depend on farm animals
They produce the most methane of any people in Africa
questions.why: Catherine says people in arid regions, like the Berbers, rely on livestock.

He likes cheese too much
He doesn't care about animals
He can't find vegan food
questions.why: Neil says he admires veganism 'but I still like cheese too much to do it!'
